title: Paris Breviary Assumption: Mary alone slew heresies; Bellatrix who crushes the serpent; Mediatrix hymns
source_text: LXII. Praeterea in Breviario Parisiensi, in Festo Assumptionis, eidem Virgini dicitur, Gaude Virgo Maria cunctas haereses sola interemisti in universo mundo. Et secunda die infra octavam Assumptionis, de eadem haec verba leguntur, Illa est quae proxime juncta Deo exercituum, meretur & ipsa suo modo, exercituum & virtutum potens vocari. Haec est nostra Bellatrix, de qua serpenti antiquo dictum est: Ipsa conteret caput tuum. Quo nomine postea narratur Rex Philippus Valesius, qui insignem victoriam de rebellibus Flandris obtinuerat, equum & arma in quibus vicerat gloriosissimae Virgini devovisse. Denique extat hymnus in fine operum Almaini, quem studiose testatur in Ecclesia Romana publice cani, in quo haec dicuntur ad Mariam Virginem, Mediatrix hominum, Ablutrix criminum, Consolatrix omnium, Peccatorum venia, Munda sordes scelerum. Ac in Litaniis illis Bonaventurae Psalterio adjectis, quarum supra facta mentio est, Virgo Maria vocatur Salus & Beatitudo, ac Cordium illuminatrix.
pass_a_gloss: Moreover in the Paris Breviary, on the Feast of the Assumption, it is said to the same Virgin: Rejoice, Virgin Mary, thou alone hast slain all heresies in the whole world. And on the second day within the octave of the Assumption these words are read of the same: She is she who, most nearly joined to the God of hosts, deserves herself also in her own way to be called powerful of hosts and virtues. This is our Warrior-woman, of whom it was said to the ancient serpent: She shall crush thy head. Under which name it is afterward narrated that King Philip of Valois, who had obtained a notable victory over the rebellious Flemings, devoted to the most glorious Virgin the horse and arms in which he had conquered. Finally there exists a hymn at the end of Almain’s works, which he carefully testifies is publicly sung in the Roman Church, in which these things are said to Mary the Virgin: Mediatrix of men, Washer-away of crimes, Consoler of all, Pardon of sinners, Cleanse the filth of wicked deeds. And in those Litanies added to Bonaventure’s Psalter, of which mention was made above, the Virgin Mary is called Salvation and Beatitude, and Illuminatrix of hearts.
pass_b_english: Paris Assumption texts: Mary alone slew all heresies; near God of hosts she is ‘our Bellatrix’ who crushes the serpent.
Philip of Valois vowed horse and arms to her after Flanders.
Public hymn: Mediatrix, washer of crimes; Bonaventure litanies: Salvation and Beatitude.

choices.why: Breviary Assumption elogium Le Blanc cites.
